messages.author: a3527f6489543e9b
messages.subject: Analysis using Neishabouri Counts
parts:
Dear GGIR community

I am interested in analysing hip-worn 24-hour accelerometer data using the Neishabouri counts function in GGIR. I have modified my previous wrist-worn accelerometry script for this purpose, but I am not sure if what I have done is correct to get the output that I want (sleep parameters analysed using Galland's algorithm and calculation of durations spent in different activity intensities using counts-based cut-points). I wonder if someone has done this before and could help me check the script below? 

GGIR(
  mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
  datadir="", 
  outputdir="", 
  do.neishabouricounts = TRUE, acc.metric="NeishabouriCount_y", do.enmo=FALSE,
  windowsizes=c(15,900,3600), #15-second epoch for the analysis
  #desiredtz="Australia/NSW",
  do.report=c(2,4,5),
  #=====================
  # Part 2
  #=====================
  strategy = 1,
  hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
  includedaycrit = 16,
  qwindow=c(0,24),
  mvpathreshold =c(25,574,1003),
  bout.metric = 6,
  #=====================
  # Part 3 + 4
  #=====================
  HASIB.algo = "Galland2012",
  Sadeh_axis = "Y",
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  includenightcrit = 16,
  #=====================
  # Part 5
  #=====================
  threshold.lig = c(25), threshold.mod = c(574), threshold.vig = c(1003),
  boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
  minimum_MM_length.part5 = 24,
  #=====================
  # Visual report
  #=====================
  timewindow = c("MM"),
  visualreport=TRUE)

Thank you in advance for your help! 

Best regards,
John.

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: Analysis using Neishabouri Counts
parts:
Hi John,

The script looks good to me. 

I have never used the Galland algorithm before in my research, but this is how it is used in GGIR. If you are using hip-worn accelerometers, consider using the "HorAngle" algorithm to define de sleep period time windows (sensor.location = "hip", HASPT.algo = "HorAngle", longitudinal_axis = 2, the longitudinal axis should be the one aligned with the spine [vertical axis], which in most brands I have seen it is the second column in the raw data, but it would be good if you double-check this in your data).

The cut-points look good, I see you are using the Evenson cut-points as provided in the manuscript, and you are using the same epoch length they used in the calibration study. Very minor point is that the calibration study reported a threshold.lig of 26, not 25, but I can't see this having a strong effect in your analyses.

Hope this helps.

Best,
Jairo

And thanks for pointing out that I've put in the incorrect cutpoint for threshold.lig. 

Thank you.

Best regards,
John.

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Analysis using Neishabouri Counts
parts:
Hi John,

Sorry for the delay in getting back to you. You are correct, you still need an algorithm to identify the sleep period time, for example the HorAngle algorithm. Your script looks fine to me. I am not aware of any study that has used the HorAngle yet.

As for the metrics, yes, setting acc.metric = ENMO and the Galland algorithm would provide physical activity using ENMO and sleep using counts.

Note also that the Galland's algorithm was developed in infants with accelerometers placed on the shin, not on the hip, just wanted to point this out as you are using hip data.

Best,
Jairo
